ai.definition: Robot Foundation Models are general-purpose AI systems that enable robots to understand visual and textual inputs and translate them into appropriate actions across a variety of tasks and robotic platforms.
ai.howItWorks: These models leverage vision-language-action datasets, which include demonstrations of various robot skills. The training process allows the model to learn transferable representations that can be applied to different tasks and robots without extensive retraining or task-specific tuning.
ai.problemSolved: Addressing the challenge of creating versatile AI-driven robotic systems capable of performing a wide range of tasks on multiple types of robots, reducing the need for specialized models per task or robot design.
ai.manufacturing: Not directly involved in manufacturing but essential for developing software and algorithms that control robotic systems.
ai.buildProcess: Involve extensive data collection, model training, and fine-tuning. The process includes gathering diverse datasets, selecting appropriate architectures, and validating performance across various tasks and robots.
ai.costDrivers: Data acquisition costs, computational resources required for training, and the need for high-performance hardware to run these models in real-time applications.
ai.lifecycleOutlook: Expected to transition from research labs into early commercial stages as foundational AI capabilities mature and more practical applications are developed.
ai.regulation: Currently no specific regulations, but will likely require compliance with general AI and robotics standards once deployed in real-world scenarios.
ai.risks: Technical risks related to model performance variability across different tasks and robots; ethical concerns regarding data privacy and bias; potential misuse of technology.
ai.profitability: Uncertain at this stage due to the research nature, but has significant potential for commercial applications as it can reduce development costs and improve robot adaptability.
ai.futureDevelopment: Expected advancements in model architectures, increased availability of diverse training datasets, and integration with other AI technologies like natural language processing (NLP) and computer vision.

glossary.def: AI models that process visual inputs and textual instructions to generate appropriate actions.
A machine learning technique where a model pretrained on one task is adapted for another related task with minimal additional training.
